tunisia.label: Tunisia
tunisia.brief: Tunisia has one of the Mediterranean's densest marina coasts, built around three natural clusters. The Gulf of Tunis wraps the capital, with the cliffside marina of Sidi Bou Said, the ferry-and-yacht port of La Goulette on the Lake Tunis sandbar, and the Gammarth beach strip. The Sahel resort coast to the south chains Yasmine Hammamet, Port El Kantaoui at Sousse and the 400-berth Cap Monastir marina along the Gulf of Hammamet. And Djerba island sits in the shallow Gulf of Gabes to the far south. Each cluster is a tight set of short water hops that today are all done by congested coast road; a fast water shuttle is the natural spine for Tunisia's tourism coast.
tunisia.corridor_shape: Three separate short-hop clusters: Gulf of Tunis (capital), Sahel resort coast (Hammamet-Sousse-Monastir), and Djerba island. Not one continuous corridor.

tunis-tunisia.name: Tunis
tunis-tunisia.brief: Greater Tunis meets the sea across the Gulf of Tunis. La Goulette, on the sandbar between Lake Tunis and the gulf, is the city's ferry and cruise gateway; a short crossing north lies Sidi Bou Said, whose marina is cut into the cliff below the blue-and-white village, and beyond it the Gammarth and La Marsa beach resorts. These waterfront points sit minutes apart by sea but are linked today only by a slow coastal road, making the bay a natural short-hop water network for the capital.

bizerte-tunisia.name: Bizerte
bizerte-tunisia.brief: Bizerte is Tunisia's northernmost city, built around a historic old port and a marina at the mouth of a lagoon channel. It anchors the north coast a short sea-run from the capital's gulf, giving the Tunis network a northern spoke.

hammamet-tunisia.name: Yasmine Hammamet
hammamet-tunisia.brief: Yasmine Hammamet is a purpose-built marina resort town on the Gulf of Hammamet, one of Tunisia's three principal wintering marinas. It is the northern anchor of the Sahel resort coast, a short water hop from Sousse and Monastir.

sousse-tunisia.name: Sousse
sousse-tunisia.brief: Sousse is the capital of the Sahel and a major Mediterranean beach destination. Its marina, Port El Kantaoui, is a purpose-built resort harbour just north of the medina, sitting mid-way on the Gulf of Hammamet resort coast between Hammamet and Monastir.

monastir-tunisia.name: Monastir
monastir-tunisia.brief: Monastir is a Sahel coastal city whose Cap Monastir Marina is one of Tunisia's largest full-service harbours, with 400 berths for yachts up to 40 metres. It anchors the southern end of the Hammamet-Sousse-Monastir resort cluster.

djerba-tunisia.name: Djerba
djerba-tunisia.brief: Djerba is Tunisia's largest island, a flat sandy resort island in the shallow Gulf of Gabes. Its main marina is at Houmt Souk on the north shore, while the Ajim ferry port on the west point is the island's historic link to the mainland. Water routes here must thread the extensive Djerba sandbanks, making a shallow-draft fast shuttle a natural fit for island and mainland connections.
